summary: Family KG, 14 staff, turnover under 2 M EUR; our ~EUR 369k is likely 18 %+ of its business, so it depends on us. Owner's costing is stale and he offered an open-book walk-through, yet on 27 Sep it demanded +7 % on the coupling hub from 1 Nov 2026, inside the fixed-price year. All three parts have a second source. Reject the increase on contract grounds, open deep for a reduction, use its own calculation and any indices that fell.
notes: Fears losing volume and is unsure of its own numbers. Increase letter cites April wage rise, energy and material, yet the owner admits he has not followed energy/material since 2022. Complains of overdue invoices although we pay ~4 days early on average (39 % >5 days late, 119 discounts taken).
fears: losing coupling hub to qualified sup:70250
losing shaft sleeve / flange share to sup:70295 / sup:70240

evidence.quote: he offered to walk us through their calculation (hourly rates and material) if that helps to settle prices.
admitted he had not followed his material and energy prices closely since the 2022 peak
Several of our invoices are overdue again. We ask you to keep to the agreed payment terms
Could you pay our invoices within 10 days? In return we would grant a cash discount.

levers: volume share on shaft sleeve and flange DN 100
arguments: contract §3.1 breach: prices fixed per calendar year, 1 Nov increase invalid
index change, only drivers that truly fell (owner has not tracked them since 2022)
rival source: sup:70250 qualified for coupling hub
avoid: accepting any part of the 7 % for 2026
tactics: First reject the 1 Nov 2026 increase: §3.1 fixes prices for the calendar year.
Accept the open-book offer and argue from its hourly rate and material shares.
If current energy/material indices are below his figures, show them; he has not tracked them since 2022.
Mention sup:70250 is qualified for the coupling hub and has free capacity.
Offer reliable on-time payment rather than paying for faster payment.
playbook.expected_concession: Renewals: asked +1.3 to +4.2 % and settled at ~0 % in 2024 and 2025; in 2023 it settled 2.0-3.6 pts below its ask.
